title: Planning, Routing & Delegation
description: Study task decomposition and dependencies, router and specialist design, shared artifacts and handoffs, and coordination cost and contention. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Task decomposition and dependencies
lessons.description: Draw a dependency graph and assign ownership of the shared configuration.
lessons.conceptOverview: Break work into outputs with explicit acceptance criteria and dependencies. Parallelize only independent steps; poorly specified subtasks create integration work that can exceed the saved execution time.
lessons.whyItMatters: Independent deliverables and clear ownership support safe parallelism.

lessons.title: Router and specialist design
lessons.description: Create routing examples that distinguish intent from keyword overlap.
lessons.conceptOverview: A router selects a constrained capability based on the task and available evidence. Define fallback behavior for ambiguous routing and measure routing errors separately from specialist performance.
lessons.whyItMatters: Routing should be evaluated on task intent and ambiguity.

lessons.title: Shared artifacts and handoffs
lessons.description: Design a handoff record that binds review to a specific artifact version.
lessons.conceptOverview: A handoff should include the task, evidence, completed work, unresolved assumptions and expected output. Shared artifacts need versioning so later workers know which state their conclusions depend on.
lessons.whyItMatters: Review and handoff decisions must identify their artifact version.

lessons.title: Coordination cost and contention
lessons.description: Choose independent partitions and a metric for coordination overhead.
lessons.conceptOverview: Additional workers introduce communication, duplicate effort and shared-resource contention. Compare end-to-end quality, latency and cost with a single-worker baseline instead of assuming more agents help.
lessons.whyItMatters: Delegation is useful only when its benefits exceed coordination costs.
